Voice commands are typically processed through two distinct machine learning approaches: one utilizing population-based data to build statistical models for speech recognition, and the other relying on individual-specific data for voice interpreter systems. The latter offers superior security and privacy compared to its counterpart. However, privacy and data acquisition challenges often prevent users from providing the substantial amounts of data required to train deep neural networks effectively for these voice interpreter systems. To address this, voice interpreter systems can leverage zero-shot learning, which enables interpretation without requiring user-provided data. This study demonstrates the efficacy of zero-shot voice interpretation using shakespeareNet, a shape-restricted neural network designed for shape-invariant learning. We evaluate the model's performance across various speech rates, showing that it achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot recognition rates of 96.6% and 95.5% for male and female speakers, respectively, when the speech rate matches that of the training data. Furthermore, the model maintains robust zero-shot interpretation even across different speech rates relative to the training set, with performance remaining within 10% accuracy. These results indicate the potential for secure and private voice command processing in real-world applications. The code and pre-trained models are accessible at https://github.com/aleksandar-k/Zero-shot-Voice-Interpretation. Additional details regarding the experiments can be found in our technical report: A. Kuzmanovic, A. Fekete, and A. K. Jain, "Zero-shot Voice Interpretation," Technical Report, arXiv preprint arXiv:2004.07003, 2020. Available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.07003. Keywords: Voice Interpretation, Shape-restricted Neural Networks, Zero-shot Learning.

We establish the existence of weak solutions with regularity $H^1(0,T; H^1(0,1))\times H^0(0,T; H^2(0,1))$ for a Coleman-Gurtin type system with boundary active tension, governed by an ordinary differential equation. The boundary active tension models spinodal decomposition and is defined as a continuous, monotone function of the order parameter's boundary values, which may vary over time. This system extends classical models featuring boundary tension. Our proof strategy relies on the surjective chain rule, Tikhonov's fixed point theorem, and monotone operator theory. Furthermore, we derive energy and dissipation inequalities. Finally, we demonstrate the existence of weak solutions satisfying these inequalities. The solution exists up to a maximal time determined by the initial data, and we analyze the corresponding blow-up phenomenon. Additionally, we investigate the well-posedness of strong solutions. These findings extend the work of [10] to include boundary active tension. Utilizing the daily probabilistic high (DPH) as a fixed point for aggregating probabilistic load forecasts enhances the accuracy of aggregate predictions for both small-scale photovoltaic (PV) systems and low-voltage grids. Additionally, calculating the conditional distribution of daily high loads (DPH) further improves forecast accuracy. This study evaluates various probabilistic load forecasting (PLF) techniques, including Monte Carlo simulations, bootstrapping, and conditional quantile regression, across multiple locations in Germany. The analysis covers scenarios with and without PV systems, comparing aggregate forecasts derived from individual appliance and low-voltage grid simulations against real-world smart meter data. Results indicate that while PLF accuracy is generally comparable across all methods, combining forecasts and identifying the conditional distribution of daily high loads yields the most significant improvements. Specifically, combining PV aggregate forecasts reduced the mean absolute error by 10% to 20%, while determining the DPH within a 5% error margin lowered the overall prediction error by 20% to 30%. These findings are expected to enhance the accuracy of probabilistic grid load forecasts. The comprehensive R package, along with simulation data and real-world measurements, is available at https://github.com/SebastianKraemer/ProbabilisticLoadForecasting. The rapid advancement of machine learning has led to significant algorithmic breakthroughs and successful real-world deployments. However, despite these successes, a substantial gap persists between current models and human cognitive capabilities. This study proposes a new research direction centered on embedding domain expertise into machine learning frameworks. We begin by examining human cognition, identifying key domain knowledge essential for human-like learning, and map these concepts onto existing machine learning principles. Subsequently, we categorize current methods for incorporating domain expertise, with a specific focus on knowledge graphs and human cognitive integration. Finally, we outline several open challenges and present a blueprint for future research aimed at enhancing machine capabilities through domain expertise integration. Given the growing complexity of machine learning systems, we argue that investigating domain knowledge integration is essential for bridging the remaining performance gap between machines and human cognition. Furthermore, this research holds significant potential for fostering interdisciplinary collaboration among researchers in machine learning, cognitive science, and neuroscience. By developing a unified framework for domain knowledge integration, this work seeks to inspire further innovation and facilitate the creation of more intelligent, human-inspired machines. Our findings and discussion are available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.01021. Accurately identifying and localizing vertebrae is essential for numerous medical tasks, including treatment planning, radiation therapy, and surgical guidance. However, image artifacts caused by patient positioning during scanning often result in misaligned spines, which hinders reliable vertebra recognition. To address this, we introduce a method that automatically rectifies the orientation of the vertebral column and enhances vertebra recognition through anatomical knowledge. Our approach first estimates the spine's orientation using a regression network trained on a large dataset of vertebra landmarks. Subsequently, we apply a linear transformation to rectify the images, followed by an anatomically-constrained enhancement step that leverages prior anatomical information to amplify the contrast between adjacent vertebrae. Finally, we train a vertebra recognition network on a large dataset of raw images, ensuring that training samples are drawn from a diverse range of spine orientations. Experimental results demonstrate that our method surpasses existing techniques in both accuracy and robustness. This work investigates the dynamical stabilization of electron vacuum oscillations under a cavity field, exploring regimes where quantum electrodynamics (QED) perturbation theory fails. We demonstrate that perturbation theory yields a divergent scattering cross-section at high energies, a divergence that disappears when employing the full non-perturbative scattering matrix (S-matrix). The resulting cross-section exhibits a resonant peak at high energies, accompanied by an exponential attenuation of the outgoing electron wave function outside the light shift resonance. This phenomenon signifies dynamical stabilization achieved through strong coupling with the cavity field, effectively shielding the electron from vacuum oscillations. This resonant behavior indicates high-energy electrons entering the cavity mode undergo elastic scattering, while those exiting are stabilized within the field. This finding offers a novel perspective on high-energy electron interactions within quantum electrodynamical regimes characterized by intense light-matter coupling. Furthermore, our findings are supported by numerical solutions to the Klein-Gordon-Dirac equations. These results have significant implications for quantum information science, quantum chemistry, and material science, as they provide a new approach to achieving dynamical stabilization via light matter coupling. Additionally, this mechanism may offer a solution to the longstanding challenge of preventing electron decay in high-energy physics. Our findings also hold relevance for high-energy particle accelerators and high-energy laser-matter interactions. Finally, the stabilization of vacuum oscillations and the associated energy shifts have potential applications in high-energy electron microscopy and electron spectroscopy. In these contexts, high-energy electrons interacting with matter exhibit resonant behavior, and the energy shifts could serve as a means to probe the electronic structure of materials. Overall, our findings provide a comprehensive understanding of electron vacuum oscillations in quantum electrodynamics and open up new avenues for research in this field. Specifically, the discovery of dynamical stabilization of vacuum oscillations and the study of electron behavior in strongly coupled light-matter regimes may lead to new applications in quantum information science, quantum chemistry, material science, and high-energy physics. Recent advancements in actuators, controllers, and sensors have accelerated the development of legged locomotion robots. Nevertheless, a significant gap persists between our sophisticated high-level planning and control algorithms and the relatively simple mechanical robot structures. This study introduces a novel machine learning framework that enables effective locomotion on complex terrains using basic robot designs featuring minimal redundancy. Our approach relies on end-to-end deep reinforcement learning, which automatically synthesizes the required actuation forces to achieve agile movement on straightforward robot models. The high-level policy selects desired foot placements to navigate the terrain, while low-level force controllers manage the actuators to execute these commands. We demonstrate the framework's efficacy by achieving robust locomotion on a 3 DOF leg with single-axis actuators across diverse and challenging environments, including a simulated rocky surface. The resulting performance on this minimalistic robot design rivals that of more complex systems with greater redundancy, such as the ANYmal locomotion platform. Furthermore, we highlight that a fundamental understanding of the robot's kinematics is unnecessary for this method. Finally, we provide an open-source implementation of the framework for simulation and hardware. This work establishes a new paradigm for the design of affordable and lightweight legged robots capable of agile locomotion on difficult terrains. The source code is accessible at: https://github.com/ashishgarg123/ElasticLoco. Our implementation is hosted on: https://github.com/ashishgarg123/ElasticLoco. We introduce a disintegration method for spin systems that avoids the common challenge of dividing them into individual spins. This approach establishes bulk properties and subsequently determines the specific spatial arrangement of spin directions. We demonstrate that this strategy yields satisfactory results for the quantum $3$-state Potts model, successfully recovering the critical exponent $\nu$ and providing a reasonable estimate for the exponent $z$. The latter finding is particularly promising, as it aligns closely with estimates derived from large-scale Monte Carlo simulations. Additionally, we present a straightforward derivation of the duality relation between $\nu$ and $z$. Finally, we outline a straightforward extension of this model, which can be viewed as a step toward a lattice version of the Fröhlich Hamiltonian. This new model exhibits a phase transition characterized by the same critical exponents, though it displays a more complex spatial structure. Specifically, in the low-temperature phase, the three-coloring of the lattice is random at the bond level but becomes ordered at the site level. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the exponents remain unchanged when the power of the coupling between operators on adjacent sites is increased. Finally, we show that the critical behavior of the lattice $\phi^4$ model can be accurately described using an analogous procedure. However, in this case, the critical exponents are not universal and depend on the specific parameters of the model. This finding is consistent with recent studies that have established the non-universality of the 3D Ising-like universality class. These results suggest that our proposed method could be highly effective for studying other models, such as the lattice gauge model. In this context, the method would enable the calculation of exponents for non-Abelian groups, thereby addressing the recent debate regarding the existence of a deconfinement transition in these systems. Our findings also contribute to the ongoing discussion concerning the potential non-existence of such a transition. Specifically, the method allows for the examination of the spatial structure of the expectation value of a string of holonomy operators, which is the key issue in the deconfinement problem. Our calculations indicate that for an odd number of sites in the extra dimension, the string breaks at the one-loop level, suggesting the presence of a deconfinement transition. Mini-scale tearing modes are anticipated to dominate magnetic reconnection in collisionless, thin current sheets across various astrophysical settings. This study examines the linear stability of such modes within a collisionless, current-sheet configuration defined by the Harris equilibrium. By extending the reduced magnetohydrodynamic (RMHD) framework to include the Hall term and employing matched asymptotic expansions, we derive a generalized Furth-Killeen-Rosenbluth (FKR) dispersion relation. We further analyze how the ion Larmor radius influences the growth rates and wavenumbers of these mini-scale modes. Finally, we validate our theoretical predictions using high-resolution Particle-in-Cell (PIC) simulations, which reveal that mini-scale tearing modes can indeed be unstable in collisionless collisionless current sheets. Additionally, we investigate the stability of both mini-scale and maxi-scale tearing modes under the influence of finite Larmor resonance (FLR). Our findings indicate that while mini-scale modes remain unstable due to the Hall term, both mini- and maxi-scale modes can become unstable when FLR effects are present. These results underscore the critical roles of both Hall and FLR effects in magnetic reconnection. The developed mini-scale tearing mode model offers a viable alternative to full PIC simulations for studying the fundamental physics of 3D magnetic reconnection in current sheets. A companion paper will address the nonlinear evolution of these mini-scale tearing modes. Our research was conducted using the open-source LSP3D code, a featureless, 3D electromagnetic particle-in-cell solver. We have made the code publicly accessible to facilitate further research on mini-scale tearing modes in collisionless slab plasmas. The visual similarity between distinct items of clothing is a core component of fashion image retrieval. However, accurately adjusting the visual characteristics of fashion features is challenging because of the significant domain gap between images from different clothing categories. To address this, we introduce a method for feature-level trait manipulation that adjusts visual attributes in unseen categories using only natural language descriptions. Our approach employs domain-adversarial training to align feature representations across multiple domains, enabling effective retrieval of manipulated item instances. Experimental results on the Shopify Clothing Dataset demonstrate that our method surpasses state-of-the-art techniques. Additionally, we find that our approach successfully generates visually coherent and semantically accurate fashion images that reflect the provided trait modifications. Identifying Banach fixed points via dual gradient ascent has emerged as a potent approach for solving variational problems within imaging science. This paper extends that methodology to address the broader category of linear ill-posed equations in Banach spaces. First, we demonstrate that the dual gradient ascent operator serves as the Banach contraction for the Kakutani fixed point, confirming convergence to the unique solution under a sufficiently small step-size. Second, under specific regularity assumptions, we prove that the method converges to the generalized solution characterized by minimal Banach norm. Finally, we present applications to classic linear ill-posed problems in Banach spaces, including Gaussian deconvolution, denoising, deblurring, and dequantization. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the method's efficacy. Notably, our approach achieves superior results in low-dose CT denoising and dequantization tasks compared to existing methods. Additionally, we enhance performance in basic problems such as Gaussian denoising and dequantization by integrating the method with the proximal point algorithm. Finally, we explore extensions of the algorithm to quasi-linear ill-posed problems. While these extensions do not guarantee convergence, numerical experiments indicate that they can yield improved outcomes in tasks like low-dose CT denoising and deblurring. Overall, this work offers a fundamental framework for a wide array of linear ill-posed equations in Banach spaces and provides a pathway for future extensions of Banach space-based imaging techniques. Our work complements recent efforts in solving linear ill-posed problems via gradient descent in Hilbert spaces. Furthermore, the proposed framework may facilitate the future extension of popular techniques, such as gradient descent ascent, to broader classes of nonlinear inverse problems. Our code is accessible at: https://github.com/zhongtao-li/DGA-IP. Keywords: nonlinear inverse problems, ill-posed problems, Banach fixed point, minimal Banach norm solution, deep image prior, deep image inverse problems.

Expense creators are rapidly emerging as a promising approach for estimating depth in light field (LF) photography. Nevertheless, most existing methods depend on a single metric, such as variance, to determine focal slices, leading to inconsistent depth estimates because they fail to account for multiple factors like occlusions. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel resilient focal slice calculator that dynamically adjusts to occlusion levels. This system utilizes a two-tier architecture: an upper tier employs a lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to detect occlusions within a frame, while a lower tier employs a regression-based algorithm to estimate camera parameters for generating focal slices. We validated our approach using various LF datasets, including those featuring occluded objects, and the results demonstrate that our method surpasses existing techniques. The source code is accessible at https://github.com/abhishekgupta1999/OCRC. Additionally, we have made the occlusion detection dataset available at https://github.com/abhishekgupta1996/Occlusion-Detection. Finally, we outline the potential of our method for applications such as holographic data storage and light field compression. This paper introduces bilinear formulations for the two-component Fokas-Lenells equations and establishes their N-soliton solutions using the Hirota method. These findings not only extend previous research but also demonstrate the broad applicability of the bilinear approach and the Hirota method in integrable systems theory. Specifically, this work derives the analytic expressions for the N-soliton solution of the Fokas-Lenells equation, a topic that has not been explored in prior literature. Within the context of optical fibers, solitons serve as critical structures for data transmission, and this study serves as a significant advancement toward a more thorough analytical grasp of soliton behavior in this domain. Furthermore, the analytical N-soliton solutions presented here are expected to prove valuable in the design and optimization of optical fiber communication technologies. Additionally, an important application of these solutions involves the study of optical pulse propagation and control. The formulas derived in this paper provide a robust foundation for modeling and simulating soliton dynamics in optical fibers, thereby offering essential support for the advancement of optical technologies. Finally, the study offers insights into the complex dynamics of N-soliton systems by exploring the interactions and collisions between multiple solitons. The bilinear N-soliton solution presented herein enables a deeper understanding of the behavior and characteristics of such systems, which is crucial for various applications in physics and engineering. Consequently, this work represents a significant contribution to the field of integrable systems and nonlinear wave phenomena. The key findings of this study are as follows: (i) We introduce the Hirota method to derive the bilinear representation and N-soliton solution for Fokas-Lenells equations. We examine a broad category of four-dimensional gravitational actions derived from three-dimensional topological deformation duals of two-dimensional holographic field theories. The classical results of this class exhibit non-linear dependencies on specific components of the Weyl curvature tensor. The corresponding dual field theories are strongly coupled and non-unitary. In contrast to other non-linear gravitational actions, the results for this class are exclusively classical. Quantum corrections are neglected because the associated central charges are infinitely large. Furthermore, these non-linear gravitational actions fail to maintain a classical unitary S-matrix. Our findings suggest that the strong holographic duality conjecture posits a one-to-one correspondence between specific features of bulk gravity and field theory, implying that specific predictions in one framework can be tested within the other. Finally, we explore the potential of using dual field theory characteristics to constrain parameters in non-Riemannian gravity. Specifically, we utilize holographic c-theorems to derive non-linear constraints for a model gravitational action of this type. Additionally, we calculate the one-loop corrections to this class of non-Riemannian gravitational actions. Surprisingly, these quantum corrections vanish, indicating that this class of non-linear gravity actions can only be consistently quantized in three dimensions. This result is consistent with expectations regarding Einstein-scalar gravity, which is the field theory dual when all deformations are absent. Our work expands the landscape of possible non-Riemannian gravitational actions and their associated field theory duals. It also provides a new avenue for testing predictions across the holographic duality. Finally, our findings offer a potential explanation for the absence of non-removable obstructions to Riemannian gravity in four dimensions. Specifically, our results suggest that non-removable obstructions to Riemannian gravity are unlikely to arise in four-dimensional gravity. Instead, these obstructions may be substituted by non-linear gravitational actions of the class we introduce. This implies that non-Riemannian gravity could manifest in the real world as a set of non-linear equations of motion for specific components of the Riemann tensor. In Home WiFi networks, clients can connect to Access Points (APs) or Extenders via their radio cards. However, selecting the most suitable AP/Extender is challenging because the signal strength indicated by the Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) does not always reflect the actual channel load of a network. To address this, we propose a method for estimating channel load using IEEE 802.11k and IEEE 802.11v protocols. This load estimation is integrated into the wireless capability information broadcast by APs/Extenders, allowing clients to consider it during association. Additionally, when roaming, IEEE 802.11v's Banned List enables clients to avoid specific APs/Extenders that are temporarily overloaded. Performance evaluations demonstrate that this approach significantly enhances Client-to-Client (C2C) throughput. Furthermore, IEEE 802.11v's Business Priority feature allows high-priority clients to preempt low-priority ones, thereby improving overall network performance. Ultimately, this solution facilitates Client-to-Client (C2C) Priority-based Service (CBS), which is essential for supporting Internet of Things (IoT) devices. Consequently, this work serves as a foundation for IEEE 802.11-based IoT systems. To the best of our knowledge, this represents the first effort to address channel load estimation and C2C CBS within the IEEE 802.11 standard. Our findings also have broader implications for the design of the next-generation WiFi standard, IEEE 802.11ax. Finally, the developed solution is open-source and available for IEEE 802.11 (WiFi) and IEEE 802.15.4 (ZigBee) implementations.
